report.title: Dev Control engineering audit
report.scope: Read-only code, configuration, workflow, and aggregate runtime-observation audit of Dev Control. No production mutation, secret access, or destructive test was performed.
report.evidence_policy: Every finding cites direct repository symbol, runtime aggregate, or official documentation evidence. Evidence is scoped to the source commit and must be revalidated before remediation.
report.redaction_policy: Credentials, environment values, ticket or prompt content, personal data, raw rows, raw logs, upload contents, and notification destinations are excluded.
report.path_note: /admin/audit remains the operational database audit-log UI; it is not a stable path for this engineering report.

product_contract.intent: Dev Control is an operator-controlled system for planning, executing, validating, reviewing, and publishing repository changes. Existing merge and deploy behavior is intentional; remediation hardens rather than removes it.
safety_invariants: Every externally visible state transition is attributable, durable, and recoverable.
Repair, review, merge, and deploy act only on approved current immutable input and target revision.
The web process does not hold broad write or deployment authority when a durable job can own it.
Public intake is validated, rate-limited, scoped, and cleaned on every failure path.
Operational status distinguishes observations from guarantees and never masks verification failure.

priority_definitions.P0: Unsafe publication/deployment, data loss, severe security, or a core workflow that lies about success.
priority_definitions.P1: Major correctness, security, or reliability risk.
priority_definitions.P2: Meaningful UX, performance, or maintainability opportunity.
priority_definitions.P3: Polish with no current material operational impact.

findings.title: Running work has no renewable ownership or automatic recovery
findings.summary: Jobs and notification deliveries are claimed without a lease heartbeat or bounded reaper.
findings.impact: Process loss or authentication refusal can strand work and leave related records stale.

evidence.observation: Job claims set claimed_at and claimed_by, but no lease expiry or heartbeat is stored or checked.
Authentication refusal updates queued jobs, while notification delivery changes a row to sending without renewable ownership or recovery.
The read-only audit observed 11 expired active sessions and 2 stale plans; these are point-in-time counts, not invariants.

findings.root_cause: Workflow ownership is represented by one-time timestamps and statuses instead of renewable leases with expiry and recovery transitions.
findings.recommendation: Add lease owner, expiry, heartbeat, and bounded reaper semantics shared by jobs and deliveries; couple recovery to ticket/run history.
acceptance_criteria: Only the live lease owner can complete or fail work.
Expired work is recovered once with an audit event.
Authentication refusal leaves every related ticket and run in an actionable terminal or queued state.
interface_changes: Expose lease expiry, owner, and recovery reason in operator APIs.

findings.title: Idempotency keys do not distinguish legitimate terminal reruns
findings.summary: Enqueue conflicts return the existing job even when its terminal history should remain immutable and a new attempt is requested.
findings.impact: A rerun can be blocked, or retry code can make failed review/conflict work look completed before replacement work succeeds.

evidence.observation: ON CONFLICT(idempotency_key) performs a no-op update and returns the pre-existing row regardless of terminal status.
Retryable handlers share the jobs-table lifecycle, so their domain status and job completion must remain correlated across attempts.

findings.root_cause: One permanent idempotency identity is used for both duplicate suppression and user-requested attempt identity.
findings.recommendation: Keep the original job immutable and create an explicitly linked rerun identity; complete domain work only after the replacement attempt succeeds.
acceptance_criteria: A terminal job can be rerun through a new linked identity.
Duplicate enqueue during an active attempt remains idempotent.
Failed review or conflict history never becomes completed merely because a retry was queued.
interface_changes: Add immutable rerun_of and attempt identity fields.

findings.title: Publication and state events are not one atomic transition
findings.summary: Several workflow paths update work state, history, and external publication in separate operations.
findings.impact: A partial failure can leave the UI, audit history, and externally visible result disagreeing.

evidence.observation: Publication performs multiple database and provider operations around commit and pull-request state rather than one durable publication state machine.
Job completion and failure update only the jobs row; related ticket/run/event updates are performed by callers.

findings.root_cause: Workflow transitions have no shared transaction/outbox boundary tying domain state, history, and external side-effect intent together.
findings.recommendation: Use a transactional state transition plus durable outbox/publication record, then make external effects idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: A database failure cannot publish an unrecorded result.
A provider failure preserves a retryable publication record and prior history.
Every externally visible transition has one attributable audit event.
interface_changes: Persist publication state and external idempotency key.

findings.title: The worker serializes unrelated job classes
findings.summary: One loop claims and awaits at most one job while also polling synchronization and notification work.
findings.impact: Throughput and recovery latency scale with the slowest operation despite operator surfaces implying general queue capacity.

evidence.observation: The loop awaits sync, delivery, one claim, and one handler sequentially before the next iteration.
The operator view reports queued/running work but has no documented single-concurrency capacity contract.

findings.root_cause: All job types share one sequential event loop without per-capability concurrency or a truthful capacity setting.
findings.recommendation: Either label the worker as single-concurrency or add bounded per-capability concurrency after lease safety is complete.
acceptance_criteria: Displayed capacity matches actual behavior.
If concurrency is enabled, independent jobs overlap without double claims.
Shutdown waits for or safely expires active leases.
interface_changes: Expose configured and observed worker capacity.

findings.title: Repair publication can reuse a prior attempt commit
findings.summary: Repair and publication paths read stored result_commit/worktree metadata that can outlive the attempt being repaired.
findings.impact: A repair can publish an old commit rather than the newly validated result.

evidence.observation: Publication initializes commit from execution_attempts.result_commit and retryPublication requires the stored commit, worktree, and branch.
Some failure paths clear result_commit, showing correctness depends on every path resetting mutable attempt state.

findings.root_cause: Mutable publication fields are reused across attempts instead of binding each repair to a fresh immutable attempt result.
findings.recommendation: Clear publication state before repair and bind validation and publication to the new attempt ID, base commit, result commit, and worktree.
acceptance_criteria: A repair cannot publish any prior attempt commit.
Publication rejects a commit not produced and validated by its attempt.
Prior attempt metadata remains immutable history.
interface_changes: Persist immutable attempt input and result identities.

findings.title: Secret scanning assumes changed paths still exist in the index
findings.summary: The validation flow can inspect staged content through git show :path even when a change deletes that path.
findings.impact: A valid deletion can fail validation or bypass consistent scanning behavior.

evidence.observation: Secret scanning derives content from changed paths and invokes Git index content reads; deleted paths need explicit handling.

findings.root_cause: The scanner models every changed path as an index blob and does not classify deletions before content inspection.
findings.recommendation: Classify change status first; scan added/modified blobs and treat deletions as content-free while retaining path-policy checks.
acceptance_criteria: A staged deletion validates without an invalid index read.
Added and modified secrets still fail closed.
Rename and binary behavior is documented and tested.

findings.title: Agent and validation children inherit worker authority
findings.summary: Claude and git validation subprocesses inherit process.env, while execution grants broad filesystem and shell tools.
findings.impact: A repository instruction or command can access credentials and capabilities unrelated to the approved task.

evidence.observation: Both invocation paths spread process.env into the child environment and add the Claude OAuth token.
Validation subprocesses use env: {...process.env}.
Execution tool policy enables filesystem and shell-capable tools rather than an OS-level authority boundary.

findings.root_cause: Child-process authority is inherited by default and prompt/tool declarations are treated as the isolation boundary.
findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit environment allowlist, separate required credentials by process role, and enforce worktree/path scope outside the prompt.
acceptance_criteria: Child environments contain only documented variables.
A repository command cannot read GitHub/deploy/notification credentials.
Agent writes outside the assigned worktree are rejected.
interface_changes: Record the operation policy and environment profile without secret values.

findings.title: Execution worktrees are not guaranteed to start fresh and be reclaimed
findings.summary: Execution can use a stale local default branch, and cleanup tooling does not prove complete lifecycle recovery.
findings.impact: Changes can be based on an obsolete revision or leave worktrees that interfere with later attempts.

evidence.observation: Worktree creation and repository validation are separate operations; a current remote default-branch proof is not persisted with the attempt.
Cleanup scans a configured directory but is not coupled to attempt lease ownership or publication state.

findings.root_cause: Worktree creation, freshness proof, ownership, and cleanup are separate conventions rather than one attempt lifecycle.
findings.recommendation: Create from a freshly verified base SHA, persist it on the attempt, and reclaim only worktrees whose attempt lease is terminal or expired.
acceptance_criteria: Attempt base SHA equals the freshly resolved protected branch SHA.
Dirty or stale repositories fail before agent launch.
Cleanup never removes a live attempt and reclaims expired terminal worktrees.
interface_changes: Expose base SHA and worktree lifecycle status.

findings.title: Conflict-resolution permissions and path scope are inconsistent
findings.summary: The conflict agent is asked to edit a worktree without a persisted allowlist limited to conflicted files.
findings.impact: It can fail to edit or modify unrelated paths while still reaching validation and publication.

evidence.observation: The prompt contains conflicted file contents and the agent runs in the full worktree; validation occurs after invocation, with no pre-invocation write allowlist persisted.
The prompt requests conflict resolution, so correctness depends on tool allowance and enforced file scope matching that request.

findings.root_cause: Prompt intent, tool permissions, and filesystem enforcement are not derived from one scoped conflict-operation policy.
findings.recommendation: Generate one policy that permits edits only to conflicted paths plus explicitly required merge metadata, and enforce it during and after execution.
acceptance_criteria: The agent can edit every conflicted file.
Writes outside the approved conflict set fail.
Remaining conflicts or unrelated diffs prevent publication.
interface_changes: Persist allowed paths and tool policy for the conflict attempt.

findings.title: Planning output finalization is not crash-safe
findings.summary: Plan files, run completion, and database plan/version rows are finalized through separate filesystem and database operations.
findings.impact: Timeout or process loss can leave a running stream, orphan plan artifact, or database row pointing at incomplete state.

evidence.observation: Planning writes prompt and plan artifacts around separate agent_run and transactional plan/version updates.
Invocation is bounded by CLI turns but has no independently persisted finalization lease tying stream completion to artifact commit.

findings.root_cause: Filesystem artifacts and run/plan state have no recoverable staging protocol with a final atomic publish marker.
findings.recommendation: Use a bounded timeout and staged artifact state; finalize the row and rename/publish artifact idempotently, with recovery for interrupted attempts.
acceptance_criteria: Timed-out planning terminates and records a final state.
A crash before DB commit leaves no active plan pointing to an orphan artifact.
Recovery finalizes or removes staged artifacts idempotently.
interface_changes: Add artifact staging/finalization status.

findings.title: Execution does not consume one immutable approved input snapshot
findings.summary: Execution re-resolves prompts, skills, project configuration, and model rather than loading one approved bundle.
findings.impact: The worker can execute inputs different from those the administrator reviewed.

evidence.observation: Execution queries current prompt versions, skills, project config, and AI configuration at run time.
Skill snapshot selection uses the earliest ticket snapshot ordered by created_at rather than an approval-bound snapshot.
Approval stores several version fields, but the execution resolver does not load one immutable approved snapshot object.

findings.root_cause: Approval metadata is recorded field-by-field while execution independently resolves effective inputs.
findings.recommendation: Persist one content-addressed approved snapshot containing plan, prompts, skills, model, project revision, and policy; execute only that snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: Preview, approval, and worker report the same input hash.
Any material input change invalidates approval.
The approved model and skill versions are used exactly.
interface_changes: Add approved_snapshot_id and input_hash to plan and execution APIs.

findings.title: Approval and rejection transitions are not one compare-and-swap
findings.summary: Status checks, version checks, metadata updates, and queueing span multiple reads and writes.
findings.impact: Concurrent approval, rejection, or revision can leave active approval metadata inconsistent with the current plan.

evidence.observation: Routes query current versions and then update ticket approval/status fields in transactions, but do not use one version-and-status compare-and-swap predicate for the complete transition.
The gate checks current version/hash/staleness, then callers perform later transitions that require their own locked recheck.

findings.root_cause: Approval state is distributed across ticket and plan fields without a single immutable approval record and CAS transition.
findings.recommendation: Create an append-only approval decision record and atomically transition only from the expected plan/status/version hash; clear all active approval references on rejection.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one concurrent decision wins.
Rejection leaves history but no active approval reference.
Execution queueing and approval consumption share the locked expected snapshot.
interface_changes: Return stable approval conflict codes and current snapshot ID.

findings.title: Skill and mandatory prompt policy is not enforced as an approved contract
findings.summary: Required skill phases, ticket override permissions, and mandatory safety instructions are resolved through separate configuration paths.
findings.impact: An execution can omit a required control or apply an override that was not visible at approval.

evidence.observation: The SQL collects global, automatic, ticket-selected, and phase-required candidates, then resolves them at runtime.
The schema stores override policy, but resolvedSkillsFor does not select or enforce allow_ticket_override.
Safety sections are prompt inputs, so their presence must be part of the approved immutable contract.

findings.root_cause: Policy sources are resolved dynamically and are not validated into one approval-bound allow/deny decision.
findings.recommendation: Resolve required skills, override permission, and mandatory safety prompts during preflight; fail closed and bind the result to the approved snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: A missing required skill blocks approval.
Disallowed ticket overrides are rejected.
Mandatory safety text cannot be disabled and its hash is visible before approval.
interface_changes: Expose policy resolution sources and hashes.

findings.title: Configuration provenance and staleness signals can diverge
findings.summary: Prompt previews, imported project updates, and validation timestamps do not all use the same versioned input identity.
findings.impact: Operators can be asked to reapprove unchanged inputs or miss a material unversioned change.

evidence.symbol: prompt-preview / project update / GitHub import routes
evidence.observation: Preview resolves current inputs; normal project updates increment config_version, while imported/synchronized fields and validation metadata follow separate update paths.
Prompt provenance stores scoped values under generic keys and is recomputed separately in web and worker code.

findings.root_cause: No canonical material-input hash separates approval-relevant configuration from operational metadata across all writers.
findings.recommendation: Define material approval inputs, version every writer that changes them, and exclude operational validation metadata from the hash.
acceptance_criteria: Material changes always change the input hash.
Validation timestamps alone never invalidate approval.
Preview and execution provenance use identical scoped keys.
interface_changes: Publish material-input hash and changed-field reasons.

findings.title: Plan ingestion depends on rigid Markdown headings
findings.summary: The parser requires a fixed ordered list of headings in generated Markdown.
findings.impact: Semantically usable plans can fail and strand workflow because of harmless formatting variation.

evidence.observation: The parser validates an exact ordered heading contract and throws invalid_plan_structure when headings differ.
The audit observed 28 failed agent runs and 2 stale plans, without attributing every count to this parser.

findings.root_cause: A presentation format is used as the machine contract instead of parsing or requesting a structured result with explicit fields.
findings.recommendation: Accept a structured plan envelope or tolerant section parser while preserving required semantic sections and human-readable Markdown.
acceptance_criteria: Required semantic sections remain enforced.
Equivalent heading punctuation/order variations do not fail.
Malformed or missing required content returns an actionable code.
interface_changes: Version the plan schema separately from Markdown rendering.

findings.title: PR discovery is owner-ambiguous and single-page
findings.summary: Open-head lookup omits owner qualification and list synchronization retrieves only one page.
findings.impact: The system can match the wrong fork branch or silently miss pull requests beyond the first page.

evidence.observation: The head query sends the supplied ref without adding owner:, and listPullRequests requests per_page=100 with no Link-page traversal.
GitHub documents owner:ref head filtering and paginated list responses.

findings.root_cause: The provider adapter treats a page and branch name as complete repository identity.
findings.recommendation: Require owner-qualified heads and traverse all Link pages with bounded cursors.
acceptance_criteria: Fork branches with equal names are distinguished.
All pages synchronize without duplicates.
Interrupted pagination resumes or reports stale partial state.
interface_changes: Expose synchronization cursor and completeness.

findings.title: Review and check truth is not materialized from authoritative APIs
findings.summary: PR list data is stored as review/check state even though the REST pull-request list does not supply complete policy inputs.
findings.impact: Operator and merge logic can act on absent, stale, or invented review/check state.

evidence.observation: Sync copies remote.review_state and remote.check_state fields from provider list results into pull_requests.
The page comments acknowledge REST PR responses do not populate review_state and falls back to internal/AI state.

evidence.location: GitHub REST reviews and review requests
evidence.observation: GitHub exposes reviews and requested reviewers through separate endpoints.

findings.root_cause: Synchronization does not aggregate reviews, requested reviewers, checks, head SHA, and source timestamps into one authoritative policy snapshot.
findings.recommendation: Fetch and store the proper review/check/reviewer/head inputs with freshness and rate-limit-aware polling or webhook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Displayed review/check state identifies its source and timestamp.
Requested reviewers and current head SHA are synchronized.
Rate limiting produces labeled stale state, not fabricated freshness.
interface_changes: Expose head SHA, policy inputs, and source freshness.

findings.title: GitHub transport policy is incomplete and inconsistent
findings.summary: REST and GraphQL paths differ in API base behavior and lack one bounded retry/timeout/version policy.
findings.impact: Enterprise/custom-base installations and transient failures can behave differently or hang without actionable state.

evidence.observation: GraphQL hardcodes https://api.github.com/graphql while REST derives an environment API base; fetch calls have no shared timeout/retry/version wrapper.
Environment fallback and validation are implemented separately from user-facing configuration documentation.

findings.root_cause: Provider requests are individual fetch calls rather than one configured transport adapter.
findings.recommendation: Centralize base URLs, API version headers, timeout, bounded retry/backoff, rate-limit metadata, and redacted errors.
acceptance_criteria: REST and GraphQL honor the configured API base.
Every request has a timeout and bounded retry policy.
Rate-limit and transport errors return stable recovery metadata.
interface_changes: Return provider freshness and retry-after metadata.

findings.title: AI review retry and verdict handling are not one idempotent state machine
findings.summary: Review invocation, comment publication, verdict parsing, and row completion are separate operations.
findings.impact: A retry can duplicate a comment or corrupt history after a partial failure, and ambiguous model output can be accepted inconsistently.

evidence.observation: The handler invokes Claude, parses a verdict, posts a comment, then updates review state through separate effects.
Verdict extraction searches a JSON block and validates selected fields, making parser strictness part of delivery state.

findings.root_cause: No idempotent review-attempt/publication record binds model output, parsed verdict, external comment, and completion.
findings.recommendation: Persist immutable review attempts and parsed envelopes before an idempotent comment outbox; never overwrite prior failure history.
acceptance_criteria: Retry after a posted comment does not post twice.
Malformed or ambiguous output fails with an actionable parser code.
Each attempt remains visible and terminal.
interface_changes: Expose review attempt and publication IDs.

findings.title: Merge is not bound to the final head SHA, required checks, and reviews
findings.summary: The merge provider call accepts repository, pull number, method, and message but no expected head SHA.
findings.impact: A head update or missing policy input can be merged after approval, making the core workflow report success for an unreviewed revision.

evidence.observation: The merge request body does not send sha and the function does not retrieve required checks/reviews immediately before merging.
The domain operation calls mergePullRequest after local state checks without passing an expected head SHA.
GitHub's merge API supports an expected head SHA and reports conflicts when it changes.

findings.root_cause: Approval and merge are not a compare-and-swap against an authoritative final GitHub policy snapshot.
findings.recommendation: Immediately re-read head, required checks, and required reviews; merge with expected SHA and record the verified snapshot and response.
acceptance_criteria: Changed head always refuses merge.
Missing or stale required checks/reviews refuse merge.
Success records the exact merged SHA and policy snapshot.
interface_changes: Require expected_head_sha and policy_snapshot_id on merge jobs.

findings.title: Successful check events can deploy a non-protected-branch SHA
findings.summary: The check_run handler passes a successful check's head SHA directly to deployment without proving it is the current protected branch head.
findings.impact: An unintended revision with a successful check can be released.

evidence.observation: A successful matching check_run calls handleDeploy with check_run.head_sha; no protected-branch head lookup precedes deployment.

findings.root_cause: Deployment authorization equates a successful named check with protected-branch membership and freshness.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the protected branch head at decision time and require exact SHA equality before creating a deployment job.
acceptance_criteria: Only the current protected branch head can deploy.
A stale or feature-branch successful check is rejected and audited.
The protected branch is explicit configuration, not an implicit checkout command.
interface_changes: Persist protected branch and verified target SHA.

findings.title: Deploy is not a health-gated recoverable release transaction
findings.summary: The script checks out master, installs dependencies, and restarts processes without migration, post-health, atomic release, or rollback stages.
findings.impact: A release can expose incompatible code or partial state and still lack a proven recovery path.

evidence.observation: The script runs git checkout/reset, pnpm install, and pm2 restart; it has no database migration, release directory swap, health gate, or rollback step.
CI uses pnpm install --frozen-lockfile while deploy.sh uses a non-frozen install.

findings.root_cause: Deployment is an in-place shell sequence rather than a staged transaction with explicit preflight, migration, health, and rollback states.
findings.recommendation: Create a staged release using the frozen lockfile, explicit migration policy, post-release health checks, and tested rollback or a clearly blocked recovery state.
acceptance_criteria: Dependency resolution is frozen.
Migration outcome is recorded before traffic/process cutover.
Failed health rolls back or blocks with tested recovery instructions.
The prior release remains recoverable.
interface_changes: Persist release stages, health evidence, and rollback target.

findings.title: Deploy lock and result state are not a durable audited history
findings.summary: PID/marker files coordinate deployment locally and can be reset after timeout or corruption.
findings.impact: A crash can leave ambiguous state, unsafe retries, or no operator-grade history of approval and outcome.

evidence.observation: Local lock, state, and exit-code marker files determine stuck recovery and completion.
Timeout-based lock reset is configured without a durable deployment attempt/lease record.

findings.root_cause: Deployment ownership, approval, retry, and outcome exist only in local mutable files rather than an append-only durable attempt model.
findings.recommendation: Represent each deployment as a leased job with immutable target/approval and append-only stage events; treat local process markers as implementation detail.
acceptance_criteria: A corrupt marker cannot authorize a new deployment.
Expired ownership is recovered once with operator-visible reason.
Approval, retry, and every stage outcome are queryable history.
interface_changes: Add deployment attempt and event records.

findings.title: Webhook and shell boundaries do not fail closed consistently
findings.summary: Request body handling, external response checks, and shell command construction use bespoke paths.
findings.impact: Oversize input, failed notification responses, or unsafe interpolation can create denial-of-service or misleading success behavior.

evidence.observation: The server accumulates and parses request bodies, notification fetch does not require an OK response, and deployment launches sh -c with constructed paths.

findings.root_cause: Untrusted HTTP data and configured paths cross request, network, and shell boundaries without one bounded validation/error contract.
findings.recommendation: Bound and reject request bodies before buffering, require checked external responses, and invoke deployment with argv rather than shell interpolation.
acceptance_criteria: Oversize bodies terminate with a stable 413 response.
External non-2xx responses are recorded as failures.
Configured paths cannot inject shell syntax.
interface_changes: Return stable webhook and notification failure codes.

findings.title: Deployment notifications have an implicit hardcoded recipient
findings.summary: The webhook server falls back to a literal phone destination when configuration is absent.
findings.impact: A deployment message can be routed to an unintended recipient and the value is embedded in source history.

evidence.observation: The destination uses process.env.WHATSAPP_PHONE || a literal phone number.

findings.root_cause: Notification destination configuration fails open to a source-coded value.
findings.recommendation: Remove the fallback, require an explicit secret-managed recipient, and fail deployment notification configuration closed without logging the destination.
acceptance_criteria: No recipient literal remains in source.
Missing recipient disables or fails notification explicitly.
Logs and audit records contain no destination value.

findings.title: Public form values are not validated against one complete field schema
findings.summary: Optional email/URL values, URL schemes, field types, and configured options are not all enforced server-side.
findings.impact: Malformed or hostile clients can bypass browser controls and store values outside the form contract.

evidence.observation: Custom validation handles public fields but does not establish one exhaustive server-side schema contract for every field type, optional value, option, and URL scheme.
Browser input types provide client hints, which are bypassable and therefore cannot be the authoritative validation boundary.

findings.root_cause: Rendering and submission validation interpret field configuration separately instead of sharing an exhaustive schema.
findings.recommendation: Compile form configuration into one validated schema used by admin save, rendering, and submission; allow only documented URL schemes.
acceptance_criteria: Present invalid optional email/URL values fail.
Select/radio/multiselect values must belong to configured options.
Unsupported field configuration is rejected before publication.
interface_changes: Return stable per-field validation codes.

findings.title: Form rendering and advertised settings diverge from implemented behavior
findings.summary: Radio, multiselect, static, attachment, CAPTCHA, notification, and rate-limit settings are not consistently rendered or enforced.
findings.impact: Operators can publish a form whose displayed controls and promised protections do not match submission behavior.

evidence.observation: The renderer maps most types to generic controls and does not implement every configured field/settings behavior.
Preview renders non-static fields through generic disabled inputs and does not demonstrate all attachment/static/multiselect behavior.

findings.root_cause: The settings model exposes capabilities without a single supported-capability registry shared by editor, preview, renderer, and server.
findings.recommendation: Create one native capability map; implement supported behavior and reject or label everything else unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Editor, preview, public form, and server agree for each supported field type.
Unsupported CAPTCHA/notification/rate/attachment settings cannot be advertised as active.
Static content is never submitted as user data.
interface_changes: Expose supported capability flags.

findings.title: Uploads are bearer identifiers without complete content and download policy
findings.summary: Upload identifiers are not bound to a form/session capability, and multipart/image/download controls are incomplete.
findings.impact: An identifier can be replayed or attached outside its intended submission, and spoofed content or unauthorized download can cross the trust boundary.

evidence.observation: Upload lifecycle is implemented through custom UUID records and filesystem paths; authorization binding and download handling are not represented as one short-lived capability.
The schema stores upload and attachment rows but no form/session capability hash or expiry boundary.

findings.root_cause: Upload identity is used as authorization instead of a scoped, expiring capability with validated content and explicit download checks.
findings.recommendation: Issue short-lived form/session-scoped capabilities, stream with size/type checks, and authorize attachment conversion and download.
acceptance_criteria: An upload cannot attach to another form/session.
Spoofed or oversize multipart content fails before persistence.
Only authorized operators can download attachments.
interface_changes: Add upload capability expiry/scope and authorized attachment metadata.

findings.title: Submission throttling trusts proxy input and counts too late
findings.summary: Rate limiting relies on derived client IP and accepted submission records rather than an atomic attempt budget.
findings.impact: Concurrent or forged requests can bypass limits or penalize the wrong client.

evidence.observation: Proxy-derived IP and submission-attempt handling are custom; accepted-workflow timing is not a single atomic consume operation.
The attempts table exists without a database-enforced atomic per-window quota.

findings.root_cause: Trusted proxy resolution and rate-budget consumption are not one configured, atomic trust-boundary operation.
findings.recommendation: Define trusted proxies and atomically consume a per-form/client attempt before validation-heavy or upload work.
acceptance_criteria: Untrusted forwarding headers do not change client identity.
Concurrent requests cannot exceed the configured budget.
Rejected attempts follow the documented counting policy.
interface_changes: Return rate-limit reset and stable error code.

findings.title: Submission failures can orphan files or silently choose a project
findings.summary: Filesystem upload creation and database submission/assignment happen across separate failure paths, with fallback project selection.
findings.impact: Failed submissions can leave artifacts, and valid input can be routed to the wrong project without operator visibility.

evidence.symbol: public submission transaction / upload cleanup / project selection
evidence.observation: The route coordinates filesystem uploads and ticket creation manually and selects project context when the form does not provide an explicit valid target.
Project assignment is nullable in the form schema, so fallback behavior must be explicit rather than silent.

findings.root_cause: Artifact compensation and assignment outcome are implicit branches around the database transaction.
findings.recommendation: Stage uploads until ticket commit, compensate every failure path, and require an explicit form/project assignment outcome.
acceptance_criteria: Every failed submission removes or expires its staged files.
DB rollback cannot leave an attached or orphan artifact.
Missing/invalid project assignment fails visibly instead of falling back.
interface_changes: Expose explicit assignment outcome and cleanup status.

findings.title: Authenticated HTTP security depends on optional runtime configuration
findings.summary: Security headers are incomplete and Secure cookies depend on NODE_ENV being set correctly.
findings.impact: A deployment configuration error can weaken session transport and browser defenses.

evidence.observation: The production flag is NODE_ENV === production and is used to conditionally secure cookies; a complete authenticated security-header policy is not centralized.
The deploy script restarts processes without proving NODE_ENV=production or other secure boot requirements.

findings.root_cause: Secure HTTP behavior is conditional and distributed instead of validated as a production boot invariant.
findings.recommendation: Fail production boot closed without secure cookie/origin configuration and centralize headers including CSP-compatible policy, frame, MIME, and referrer controls.
acceptance_criteria: Production cannot start with insecure cookie configuration.
Authenticated responses include the documented header baseline.
Development behavior is explicit and separately tested.
interface_changes: Expose non-secret secure-config health fields.

findings.title: Session, CSRF, proxy, and login-throttle controls are not one hardened boundary
findings.summary: Expired session cleanup, proxy identity, username lockout behavior, and CSRF comparison use separate custom logic.
findings.impact: Attackers can target accounts for denial of service, influence client identity, or exploit inconsistent token handling.

evidence.observation: Authentication uses custom session, login-attempt, proxy-IP, and CSRF logic; CSRF hashes are compared as strings rather than one constant-time byte comparison path.
Session expiry and login attempts are stored, but the schema does not schedule cleanup or define an account-safe throttle policy.

findings.root_cause: Authentication protections are implemented as independent route checks without one threat-modeled session and client-identity policy.
findings.recommendation: Use trusted-proxy client identity, constant-time token comparison, expiry cleanup, and throttling that limits sources without enabling permanent username-targeted lockout.
acceptance_criteria: Expired sessions are rejected and cleaned.
CSRF comparison uses equal-length constant-time bytes.
Forwarding-header spoofing fails.
One attacker cannot lock out a username globally.
interface_changes: Return stable auth failure classes without account disclosure.

findings.title: Secret storage and redaction accept literal credentials
findings.summary: Notification configuration can store authorization headers directly and error redaction covers only selected paths.
findings.impact: Secrets can persist in JSON, logs, or returned errors beyond the intended secret boundary.

evidence.observation: Configuration accepts authorization_header directly as well as a secret reference.
The write route accepts authorization_header, while the response helper only hides it from selected output.
Notification error redaction is provider-specific rather than a process-wide structured logging policy.

findings.root_cause: Credential values are allowed in general configuration and redaction is applied after errors are formatted.
findings.recommendation: Require secret references or encrypted storage, remove literals, and apply structured allowlisted error/log serialization before persistence or response.
acceptance_criteria: Literal credentials are rejected.
Known secret canaries never appear in rows, logs, or responses.
Rotation changes a reference without rewriting unrelated config.
interface_changes: Expose only secret reference identifiers and configured booleans.

findings.title: Web handlers hold direct GitHub write and deployment authority
findings.summary: Authenticated web routes can perform provider mutations instead of only enqueueing durable least-privilege jobs.
findings.impact: A web-process compromise can gain broad repository or deployment side effects.

evidence.observation: The web server imports provider operations and owns routes that trigger review/merge or other GitHub-related mutations.
Merge is a callable domain/provider side effect rather than exclusively a worker job boundary.

findings.root_cause: Process roles are divided by convention while the web process retains credentials and direct write call paths.
findings.recommendation: Give web only read/enqueue capability; execute GitHub writes and deploys in audited jobs with narrower credentials and policy checks.
acceptance_criteria: Web runs without GitHub write or deployment credentials.
Every write has a durable job, actor, approved target, and idempotency key.
Worker credentials are scoped to the exact provider operations required.
interface_changes: Publish process-role capability health without credential values.

findings.title: Password tooling leaks arguments and compiles native code at runtime
findings.summary: Admin creation accepts a password command-line argument and the password module compiles a C helper into /tmp during module load.
findings.impact: Passwords can appear in process history, long/newline edge cases can truncate, and authentication can fail on hosts without compiler/runtime libraries.

evidence.observation: The non-interactive CLI reads the password from a command-line flag.
The module invokes gcc at runtime and passes newline-delimited password input to a helper.
The helper uses a fixed 4096-byte line buffer.

findings.root_cause: Password input and hashing portability are delegated to ad hoc CLI/native process conventions.
findings.recommendation: Read secrets from stdin or a protected file descriptor, reject unsupported edge cases explicitly, and package/document a reproducible Argon2 runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Password never appears in argv.
Length/newline behavior is explicit and tested.
Production authentication starts without a compiler and with pinned Argon2 support.
interface_changes: Document supported password input contract.

findings.title: Notification providers receive events without persisted rule evaluation
findings.summary: Enqueue creates deliveries for every enabled provider, while the event union and admin rule list cover different subsets.
findings.impact: Providers can receive unintended events or miss expected workflow events.

evidence.observation: The event union is a fixed subset and enqueueNotification inserts for every enabled provider without a rule predicate.
The UI lists enabled and disabled event names that are not represented as persisted provider routing rules.

findings.root_cause: Event taxonomy and provider routing policy are UI/code constants instead of versioned persisted rules evaluated at enqueue time.
findings.recommendation: Define one event registry and per-provider allow rules; reject unknown events and record the matched rule.
acceptance_criteria: A provider receives only enabled events.
All emitted workflow events exist in the registry.
Rule changes are audited and do not rewrite prior deliveries.
interface_changes: Add event_type, matched_rule_id, and taxonomy version.

findings.title: Delivery retry budgets and sending recovery ignore provider policy
findings.summary: The worker retries failed rows indefinitely on a fixed backoff and sending rows have no lease recovery.
findings.impact: Failed or crashed sends can retry beyond configuration or remain stuck forever.

evidence.observation: Selection includes queued/failed but not expired sending rows; update increments attempt_count and reschedules without reading provider max_attempts.
The UI exposes max attempts although the worker delivery path does not enforce it.

findings.root_cause: Delivery state lacks lease expiry and a terminal retry-budget transition tied to provider configuration.
findings.recommendation: Lease sending deliveries, enforce a validated max-attempt count, and move exhausted deliveries to a terminal actionable state.
acceptance_criteria: Expired sending recovers once.
No delivery exceeds its configured attempts.
Exhaustion is terminal and operator-visible.
interface_changes: Expose delivery lease and terminal reason.

findings.title: Manual retry can race the worker and duplicate a send
findings.summary: The admin retry route calls the provider directly without acquiring the worker's delivery transition.
findings.impact: One delivery can be sent twice and receive conflicting final status updates.

evidence.observation: The route fetches a delivery, invokes provider.send directly, and updates it without a compare-and-swap ownership predicate.
The worker independently claims eligible rows and performs the same send side effect.

findings.root_cause: Manual and automated delivery paths bypass a shared leased idempotent send command.
findings.recommendation: Make manual retry enqueue or transition the same delivery job under CAS; use a stable provider idempotency key where supported.
acceptance_criteria: Manual retry never sends concurrently with a worker.
Repeated clicks create at most one external send.
Status history identifies the retry actor and attempt.
interface_changes: Return retry job ID instead of synchronous provider result.

findings.title: Provider endpoint, method, timeout, and credential configuration is weakly validated
findings.summary: Configuration accepts parseable URLs, arbitrary methods/timeouts/headers, and literal authorization values.
findings.impact: Misconfiguration can leak credentials, target unintended endpoints, or create unbounded delivery behavior.

evidence.observation: Endpoint validation is URL parsing; method, timeout, headers, and direct authorization_header values feed fetch behavior.
Numeric and credential configuration is accepted from request fields with limited cross-field policy validation.

findings.root_cause: Provider configuration is treated as transport options rather than a validated outbound-request security policy.
findings.recommendation: Allow only supported HTTPS destinations/methods, bound timeout and attempts, require secret references, and test without external sends.
acceptance_criteria: Non-HTTPS or disallowed destinations are rejected.
Timeout and attempts stay within documented bounds.
Test sends use the same validation and leave normal delivery state unchanged.
interface_changes: Expose validated provider capabilities, not raw credentials.

findings.title: Migration execution is neither serialized nor uniquely ordered
findings.summary: The runner checks/applies files without an advisory lock, and migration filenames can share numeric prefixes.
findings.impact: Concurrent deploys or ambiguous ordering can diverge database schema state.

evidence.observation: The runner creates schema_migrations and loops files without a PostgreSQL advisory lock.
The directory contains numeric migration naming managed only by full filename uniqueness, not a unique monotonic prefix policy.

findings.root_cause: Migration coordination and ordering rely on deployment convention rather than a database lock and validated naming rule.
findings.recommendation: Acquire a transaction/session advisory lock, validate unique monotonic prefixes, and fail before applying an ambiguous set.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent migration processes serialize.
Duplicate or out-of-order prefixes fail before DDL.
A failed migration leaves an actionable recorded state.
interface_changes: Document migration lock key and naming contract.

findings.title: Core status and append-only invariants rely on application code
findings.summary: Several tables store free-form statuses or audit/provenance rows without complete database-enforced lifecycle constraints.
findings.impact: A bug or maintenance query can create impossible transitions or delete required history.

evidence.observation: Multiple workflow status columns are text without table-level state/data checks, and audit history is not protected from deletion.
Some hash/scope constraints exist, demonstrating that other lifecycle invariants can also be enforced at the DB boundary.

findings.root_cause: The database is treated as storage while workflow validity and append-only guarantees live mainly in callers.
findings.recommendation: Add targeted CHECK/foreign-key/trigger protections for stable invariants and review indexes against actual high-value queries before adding any.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid stable statuses and broken required relationships fail in PostgreSQL.
Append-only audit/provenance deletion is blocked or tightly privileged.
Every added index is justified by an EXPLAIN-backed query.
interface_changes: Document database-enforced invariants.

findings.title: Filesystem artifacts and database references are not atomically published
findings.summary: Plan, log, upload, and worktree artifacts are written outside PostgreSQL transactions that reference them.
findings.impact: Crashes can create orphan files or live rows with missing content.

evidence.observation: Filesystem paths are created and then stored in run/plan/attempt metadata across separate operations.
Upload files and attachment/database rows require manual compensation across failure paths.

findings.root_cause: Artifact lifecycle has no shared staged/finalized state or reconciliation job across filesystem and database boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Write to staged identities, commit the row, atomically rename/finalize, and reconcile expired staged or missing artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: No active row points to a missing artifact after recovery.
Expired staged files are removed safely.
Finalized artifacts have an integrity hash and owner record.
interface_changes: Add artifact state, owner, hash, and finalization timestamp.

findings.title: Backup and retention claims do not cover complete tested recovery
findings.summary: The backup script dumps PostgreSQL only, while filesystem artifacts/configuration, scheduling, retention, and restore verification are separate or absent.
findings.impact: A nominal backup can be unusable for restoring the service's full state.

evidence.observation: The script runs pg_dump to data/backups and does not manifest artifact/configuration content or perform a restore verification.
Operator surfaces expose operational configuration but do not provide a verified restore result or implemented scheduler contract.

findings.root_cause: Backup is a database command rather than a versioned full-service recovery product with lifecycle and drill evidence.
findings.recommendation: Create a manifest for database, required artifacts, and configuration references; implement truthful retention/scheduling and an isolated restore drill.
acceptance_criteria: Manifest covers DB, artifacts, and configuration references.
Retention and schedule match the displayed contract.
An isolated restore verifies service health and records the result.
interface_changes: Add backup/restore manifest and verification record.

findings.title: Worker health is inferred from job activity
findings.summary: Dashboards use the latest job claimed_at and configured values rather than a renewable worker heartbeat.
findings.impact: An idle healthy worker can look stale and a dead worker can look healthy after recent activity.

evidence.observation: Worker heartbeat is SELECT MAX(claimed_at) from jobs.
Operate derives worker identity/time from claimed job rows rather than a worker lease.

findings.root_cause: Activity timestamps are used as health signals because workers have no renewable identity/heartbeat record.
findings.recommendation: Persist worker heartbeat, capability, version, and lease freshness separately from job activity.
acceptance_criteria: Idle live workers remain healthy.
Dead workers become unhealthy after the documented interval.
Health identifies supported capabilities and timestamp source.
interface_changes: Expose heartbeat freshness and worker capability set.

findings.title: Settings and GitHub health advertise capabilities they do not prove
findings.summary: Operator settings describe limits, cleanup, backups, or merge behavior not implemented by the underlying paths, and GitHub health checks configuration rather than the needed capability.
findings.impact: Operators can rely on a control that is inactive or mistake a configured URL/token for working authority.

evidence.observation: The page renders environment/configuration-derived operational values and GitHub configuration state.
GitHub status is derived from whether GITHUB_API_BASE_URL is present, not an authenticated read/write capability probe.
The implemented backup behavior is narrower than a complete retention/restore capability.

findings.root_cause: UI labels are sourced from configuration intent instead of verified implementation/capability status.
findings.recommendation: Remove unsupported settings or label them unavailable; probe the exact required GitHub capability with freshness and no mutation.
acceptance_criteria: Every setting maps to an implemented behavior or is explicitly unavailable.
GitHub health distinguishes read, write, and merge capability without mutating remote state.
Capability status includes source and freshness.
interface_changes: Expose capability status, reason, and checked_at.

findings.title: Run progress and pull-request staleness are not represented
findings.summary: Agent runs store status but progress is not updated, and synchronized PR data lacks visible source staleness.
findings.impact: Operators cannot distinguish slow progress from a stuck run or current PR state from old cached data.

evidence.observation: Run rows move between running and terminal states, but no periodic progress field is updated during invocation.
Stored PR fields are updated from polling results without a completeness/freshness contract surfaced to operators.

findings.root_cause: Long-running work and cached provider state have coarse statuses but no renewable progress/freshness model.
findings.recommendation: Record bounded progress events/heartbeat and display PR source timestamp, completeness, and stale threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Running work updates progress or heartbeat at a documented cadence.
Stale PR data is visibly labeled.
Progress never fabricates percent completion when only phase is known.
interface_changes: Add run phase/heartbeat and PR source freshness.

findings.title: Repair history and list/log reads are not durable or paginated
findings.summary: Repair can replace log linkage, while many list pages cap rows or load logs without a cursor contract.
findings.impact: Historical evidence becomes inaccessible and operators silently miss older records or load unbounded content.

evidence.observation: Each attempt stores log_path in mutable run metadata; repair history depends on preserving every run link.
Ticket list orders results and applies LIMIT 200 without a pagination cursor.
Delivery history uses LIMIT 200 without a pagination contract.
Audit log UI is the operational DB-backed /admin/audit surface and uses LIMIT 200; it is not the static engineering audit report.

findings.root_cause: History is addressed through mutable latest-run metadata and fixed caps instead of immutable artifact references plus cursor pagination.
findings.recommendation: Preserve one log artifact per attempt and paginate every list/log endpoint with bounded page sizes and stable cursors.
acceptance_criteria: Every repair retains links to prior logs.
Every list/log API documents limit and cursor.
Browsing all pages returns each record once under stable ordering.
interface_changes: Add immutable log artifact ID and pagination cursors.

findings.title: Read routes mutate workflow and errors lack stable recovery contracts
findings.summary: Ticket detail GET can change ticket status, while many errors return text without stable codes and next actions.
findings.impact: Refreshing a page can alter state and operators cannot automate or reliably recover from failures.

evidence.observation: The GET render path updates early ticket state/history when the detail page is viewed.
Routes frequently return or throw message strings; stable error codes and recovery metadata are not centralized.

findings.root_cause: HTTP method semantics and operational error taxonomy are not enforced by shared route boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Make GET side-effect-free; move acknowledgement to an explicit audited command and return stable code/message/recovery fields.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated GETs make no database changes.
Viewing requires no hidden status transition.
Every surfaced operational error has a stable code and actionable recovery step.
interface_changes: Standardize error_code and recovery_action.

findings.title: Tabs and mobile navigation lack complete keyboard/focus semantics
findings.summary: Tabs respond to clicks without roving focus keys, and mobile navigation does not expose expanded state or Escape behavior.
findings.impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users can lose context or fail to operate navigation efficiently.

evidence.observation: The handler toggles aria-selected and hidden panels on click but has no Arrow/Home/End focus movement.
The opener toggles sidebar and scrim without aria-expanded/aria-controls synchronization or Escape close handling.

findings.root_cause: Interactive behavior implements pointer visibility changes without a shared keyboard and focus-management contract.
findings.recommendation: Implement native ARIA tab keyboard behavior and explicit mobile nav expanded/focus/Escape lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: Tabs support Arrow, Home, End, and activation semantics.
Opening nav moves or preserves focus predictably and updates aria-expanded.
Escape closes and restores focus.

findings.title: Responsive layouts and touch targets are incomplete
findings.summary: Some grids retain fixed desktop columns, data rows lose labels on small screens, and some controls lack two-dimensional target sizing.
findings.impact: Small-screen and touch users can encounter horizontal overflow or ambiguous unlabeled values.

evidence.observation: Mobile rules hide list headers and set minimum height for common controls but do not supply labels for every specialized grid or minimum width for all interactive components.
Several controls use min-width:600px or fixed repeated columns.
Merge target inputs use fixed inline width values.

findings.root_cause: Desktop grid structure is reused responsively without component-level labels, wrapping rules, and target-size guarantees.
findings.recommendation: Add per-row labels or semantic tables, remove page-level fixed-width overflow, and guarantee supported touch target dimensions.
acceptance_criteria: No horizontal page overflow at supported mobile widths.
Every compact row retains its field labels.
Interactive targets meet the documented minimum size.

findings.title: Animations ignore reduced-motion preference
findings.summary: The design tokens define pulsing and entrance animations without a prefers-reduced-motion override.
findings.impact: Motion-sensitive users cannot ask the interface to suppress nonessential animation.

evidence.observation: Animation keyframes and uses exist, but the stylesheet has no prefers-reduced-motion: reduce rule.

findings.root_cause: Motion is encoded as unconditional component styling rather than a user-preference-aware token.
findings.recommendation: Add a global reduced-motion override that removes smooth scrolling and minimizes nonessential animation/transition duration.
acceptance_criteria: Reduced-motion mode disables smooth scrolling and nonessential animation.
State changes remain perceivable without motion.

findings.title: Attachments are not surfaced consistently in preview and operator flows
findings.summary: Form preview does not represent attachment controls, and ticket/operator detail does not expose a complete authorized attachment affordance.
findings.impact: Users cannot confirm configured attachment behavior or retrieve submitted evidence.

evidence.observation: The preview renders every non-static field as a generic disabled input, not an attachment-specific control.
The detail page renders ticket fields, plans, runs, and activity without an attachment section.

findings.root_cause: Attachment metadata/download authorization is not part of the shared form and ticket view model.
findings.recommendation: Expose authorized attachment metadata and render native upload/preview/download affordances consistently.
acceptance_criteria: Form preview identifies attachment fields.
Authorized ticket detail lists attachments with safe metadata.
Unauthorized users receive no attachment content or path.
interface_changes: Add authorized attachment metadata to form/ticket view models.

findings.title: Inline assets and external fonts constrain CSP and privacy
findings.summary: Every document emits inline style/script content and Google Fonts requests.
findings.impact: A strict CSP is difficult to deploy and every page adds third-party font latency and privacy exposure.

evidence.observation: The document helper emits external Google Fonts links plus inline style and script content.
Most visual styling already has a local stylesheet home, so inline styles can be migrated incrementally without a new framework.

findings.root_cause: The document renderer treats scripts/styles/fonts as per-page strings instead of local CSP-compatible assets and tokens.
findings.recommendation: Move reusable inline content to local assets, use nonce/hash only where necessary, and prefer system/local fonts; retain minor accent-border cleanup as P3 token maintenance rather than a separate cosmetic finding.
acceptance_criteria: Pages run under the documented CSP without unsafe-inline where avoidable.
No external font request is required.
Visual regression checks cover changed tokens and WCAG-conscious contrast.

findings.title: CI explicitly masks Vitest failure
findings.summary: The CI test step converts a failing Vitest process into a successful shell command.
findings.impact: Regressions can merge while the required check reports success.

evidence.observation: pnpm exec vitest run is followed by || echo, which produces a zero exit status after failure.

findings.root_cause: The workflow treats test failure as optional tool absence instead of distinguishing configuration setup from a failing test run.
findings.recommendation: Run the scoped product suite directly and let every failure fail the job.
acceptance_criteria: An intentional failing test makes CI fail.
The scoped product suite command matches the documented local command.
Missing test setup fails with actionable output.
interface_changes: Document one root verification command.

findings.title: Critical boundaries lack focused integration coverage
findings.summary: The suite has unit tests but no meaningful route/worker/database/webhook/upload journey coverage, while Playwright is installed but unused.
findings.impact: High-risk regressions at transaction and process boundaries can escape green unit tests.

evidence.observation: @playwright/test is installed.
CI runs installation, TypeScript, and Vitest only; no browser or boundary journey step exists.

findings.root_cause: Verification is organized around modules rather than the few high-risk trust and state transitions.

Browser artifacts are optional, redacted, and bounded.

findings.title: Tooling and workspace setup are not reproducible from one contract
findings.summary: Action/tool versions, production scripts, workspace dependency declarations, and setup prerequisites are scattered.
findings.impact: A clean machine or deploy host can resolve different tools or fail on undocumented native requirements.

evidence.observation: There is no single root verify script covering the requested scoped contract, and tool versions use range declarations.
CI setup and versions live in workflow steps rather than one documented workspace prerequisite contract.
Authentication has an undocumented native compiler/library prerequisite at runtime.

findings.root_cause: Reproducibility information is distributed across package manifests, CI, deploy scripts, and runtime code.
findings.recommendation: Define one root verify command and document/pin the minimum Node/pnpm/native/workspace prerequisites used by CI and production.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh documented setup runs verification without undeclared prerequisites.
CI and production use the same frozen dependency graph.
Native runtime requirements are prebuilt or explicitly checked at startup.
interface_changes: Publish workspace prerequisite and verification contracts.

findings.title: Placeholder scripts and empty packages advertise nonexistent capability
findings.summary: Repository entry points exist without complete behavior.
findings.impact: Operators and developers can invoke a command or package that appears supported but does not perform the promised lifecycle.

evidence.observation: Cleanup exists as a standalone scan without the attempt ownership/recovery guarantees implied by lifecycle cleanup.
Workspace discovery includes package directories regardless of whether they expose a meaningful supported contract.

findings.root_cause: Scaffolding was retained as product surface before its behavior and ownership contract were complete.
findings.recommendation: Delete misleading entry points or implement only the currently required behavior with a focused check.
acceptance_criteria: Every advertised script/package has a documented supported outcome and verification.
Unused empty surfaces are removed without replacement abstractions.

findings.title: Web and worker duplicate input resolution logic
findings.summary: Both processes resolve prompts, skills, and AI configuration through separate implementations.
findings.impact: The preview and execution paths can drift even when each local test passes.

evidence.observation: The web server resolves skill and prompt preview inputs.
The worker contains a separate resolver with its own provenance behavior.

findings.root_cause: A shared domain rule is copied into process modules rather than reused from one tested pure resolver/query boundary.
findings.recommendation: Extract only the common input-resolution contract and parity tests; keep process-specific I/O in place.
acceptance_criteria: Web preview and worker execution produce identical hashes for the same fixture.
There is one implementation of resolution precedence.
No speculative framework or dependency is added.
interface_changes: Expose one resolved-input contract.

findings.title: Oversized process modules inhibit boundary testing
findings.summary: Primary web, worker, and UI files combine routing, persistence, rendering, provider, and workflow concerns.
findings.impact: Small changes require broad context and make focused failure injection difficult.

evidence.observation: One large module owns many unrelated admin/public routes and shared helpers.
One large module owns planning, execution, publication, GitHub review/conflict, notifications, polling, and dispatch.
One module combines document rendering and many inline client behaviors.

findings.root_cause: Process entry modules accumulated unrelated responsibilities without extraction at tested state or trust boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Split only where current remediation needs a test seam: route commands, worker handlers, and reusable client assets; avoid broad architectural rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: High-risk handlers can be tested without booting unrelated services.
Entrypoints remain thin and behavior-compatible.
Extraction follows existing module patterns and adds no dependency.
